tagline: Cattle roads and power projects became a journey through the high Sierra.
intro: The Sierra Vista Scenic Byway links high meadows, granite domes and the San Joaquin River canyon in the Sierra National Forest. The Forest Service describes a 100-mile drive taking about five hours, highlighting Sierra Nevada scenery and views. Designated a National Forest Scenic Byway in July 1989, it joined a program created to give access to scenic, recreational and historic features.

A motor road reached Beasore Meadows in 1925, generally following livestock routes to summer grazing country. Minarets Road grew from a separate road improved during construction of Southern California Edison's Mammoth Pool hydroelectric project in the 1950s. A proposed extension across the Sierra to Mammoth Lakes passed a federal feasibility study in 1957 but was never built. The byway designation also aimed to support nearby rural economies. Local residents formed the Sierra Vista Scenic Byway Association in 1990 to promote and develop the route.

Driving from the Oakhurst side, the route climbs Sky Ranch Road from Highway 41, passes Nelder Grove and Fresno Dome, and reaches Cold Springs Summit. Continue through Beasore Meadows toward Mammoth Pool Reservoir and Mile High Vista, then descend Minarets Road toward North Fork. The 2020 Creek Fire damaged roads and bridges; rehabilitation of approximately 70 miles was contracted in 2025.

moments.title: Cold Springs Summit
moments.text: At 7,308 feet, Cold Springs Summit is the highest point on the byway. A short trail leads from the summit to Cold Springs Meadow, with views toward Madera Peak. The route connects the summit with Beasore Road and its high-elevation meadows on one side, and Fresno Dome and Nelder Grove on the other.
moments.notice: The trail to Cold Springs Meadow has views toward Madera Peak.

moments.title: Beasore Meadows
moments.text: Beasore Meadows lies east of Bass Lake, where cattlemen used the high meadows as summer range. A motor road opened in 1925, generally following livestock routes into the mountains. That road later became part of the Sierra Vista Scenic Byway. The byway follows Beasore Road through the meadows before turning south toward Cold Springs Summit.

moments.title: Mile High Vista
moments.text: Mile High Vista looks over the San Joaquin River canyon and Mammoth Pool Reservoir, with the Minarets and Mount Ritter visible beyond. The road serving this view developed alongside the reservoir project: in the 1950s, access roads were built through the canyon to the dam and powerhouse sites. The Creek Fire later killed extensive areas of forest along the route, exposing terrain and distant views previously screened by trees. Roads and bridges were damaged too: Norris Creek Bridge was destroyed, and by May 2021 the Forest Service reported that the complete byway loop could not be driven.
moments.notice: Mammoth Pool Reservoir lies below the viewpoint; the Minarets and Mount Ritter are visible from it.

practical: Cold Springs Summit: High sections are not plowed in winter. The usual season is June through October, depending on snow and road conditions. (checked 2026-10-11)

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Sierra National Forest Scenic Drives
